source_refs.note: The Ripple Tank: a main subheading of 7.8 Diffraction of waves, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 157-158.

blocks.text: Fig. 7.11 shows a ripple tank. It is a very useful apparatus not only to generate water waves, but also to demonstrate wave properties (such as reflection, diffraction and refraction).

blocks.alt: A ripple tank: a glass bottomed tray of water in a frame on four legs. A vibrator bar hangs by elastic bands from wooden bars on a stand and touches the water surface. A lamp on the stand shines down from above, and a white screen on the floor below shows the wave pattern. Labels: Lamp, Stand, Vibrator, Water surface, Elastic bands, Frame, Glass bottomed tray, Leg, Wave pattern on screen, White screen.
blocks.caption: Figure 7.11: A ripple tank (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 7.11).

blocks.text: Ripple tank contains water, vibrator (e.g. a motorized oscillating needle), obstacles (e.g. a small rectangular block or a semicircular barrier) and gap widths of different sizes. It creates a series of concentric circles or parallel waves using the vibrator. An obstacle is placed for creating a gap with a specific width. The experiment can be repeated with different gap widths.

blocks.alt: Two diagrams with straight wavefronts reaching a gap in a barrier. Left: a narrow gap, and the waves beyond spread in half circles: Small gap, Increased diffraction. Right: a wide gap, and the waves beyond stay mostly straight, curving only at the edges: Large gap, Decreased diffraction.
blocks.caption: Small gap, increased diffraction; large gap, decreased diffraction (original drawing after the diagrams printed with the textbook's Figure 7.11).

blocks.text: It is observed that when the gap width is small compared to the wavelength, diffraction is significant and the waves bend around the obstacle, creating a semicircular pattern. As the gap width increases relative to wavelength, diffraction decreases and the waves pass through the gap with less bending.

blocks.title: For your Information
blocks.text: Diffraction of white light is shown by a fine diffraction grating.
This experiment demonstrates the qualitative effect of gap width on diffraction in a ripple tank, illustrating how the relationship between gap width and wavelength affects wave behaviour.

blocks.title: Example 7.6
blocks.problem: In a ripple tank, a wave generator produces 500 pulses in 10 s. Find the frequency of the pulses produced?

blocks.title: Interesting Information
blocks.text: The fine rulings, each 0.5 μm wide, on a compact disc function as a diffraction grating. When a small source of white light illuminates a disc, the diffracted light forms coloured lanes that are composite of the diffraction patterns from the rulings.
